results.trace: tests/sim/rival-pickup-block.test.ts:12-18 steerTo(car, p) = clamp(wrap(atan2(p.x-car.x, -(p.z-car.z)) - car.heading) * 2.5, -1, 1), using hand-rolled while-loop wrap and Math.max/min clamp. tests/sim/helpers.ts:163-168 driveToward(world, x, z, carIndex=0) returns steer = clamp(wrapAngle(headingOf(x-car.x, z-car.z) - car.heading) * 2.5, -1, 1). src/sim/vec.ts:19-21 headingOf(dx,dz) = Math.atan2(dx,-dz), the same formula. vec.ts:10 wrapAngle wraps to (-π, π], vec.ts:5 clamp. The CarView that steerTo reads comes from carViews(world)[0] -> carView (src/sim/car.ts:142-155), which copies x: car.x, z: car.z and heading: car.heading straight from world.cars[0]. So it reads the same inputs driveToward reads. Wrap conventions differ only at exactly ±π, where 2.5·π gets clamped to ±1 either way. The `drive` callback already gets `world`, and the file already imports from './helpers.ts' (dustBowl). steerTo duplicates driveToward(world, box.x, box.z).steer.
results.reason: The new test-only steerTo duplicates the existing driveToward helper in tests/sim/helpers.ts (same heading formula, wrap, gain 2.5 and clamp) and hand-rolls helpers from vec.ts. Replacing it gives the same steer values.

results.reason: The code is correct (boost is per car), so a test of it would pass on this branch and can't fail. AC3's test matches the spec's own wording. This is a coverage or mutation-testing suggestion, not a defect.
